officialTitle: Tepotinib in Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer with MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutations

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: As of January 1, 2020, a total of 152 patients had received tepotinib, and 99 patients had been followed for at least 9 months.
primaryEndpoints: ORR by independent review (≥9 months follow-up)

clinicalQuestion: What is the activity of tepotinib in advanced NSCLC with MET exon 14 skipping detected by liquid or tissue biopsy?

pico.population: Advanced or metastatic NSCLC with confirmed MET exon 14 skipping mutation (liquid or tissue biopsy)
pico.outcomes: Primary: ORR by independent review. Secondary: DoR, response by biopsy method, safety

arms.label: Tepotinib
arms.doseSourceQuote: we administered tepotinib (at a dose of 500 mg) once daily

publications.title: Tepotinib in Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer withExon 14 Skipping Mutations.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: The response rate by independent review was 46% (95% confidence interval [CI], 36 to 57), with a median duration of response of 11.1 months (95% CI, 7.2 to could not be estimated) in the combined-biopsy group.

The response rate by independent review was 46% (95% confidence interval [CI], 36 to 57), with a median duration of response of 11.1 months (95% CI, 7.2 to could not be estimated) in the combined-biopsy group.
The response rate was 48% (95% CI, 36 to 61) among 66 patients in the liquid-biopsy group and 50% (95% CI, 37 to 63) among 60 patients in the tissue-biopsy group

safety.sourceQuote: Adverse events of grade 3 or higher that were considered by investigators to be related to tepotinib therapy were reported in 28% of the patients, including peripheral edema in 7%.

safety.description: Permanent discontinuation due to adverse events
safety.sourceQuote: Adverse events led to permanent discontinuation of tepotinib in 11% of the patients.

strengths: Prospective comparison of liquid and tissue biopsy detection

clinicalImplications.text: Supports tepotinib for MET exon 14 skipping NSCLC and validates plasma ctDNA testing as a route to identifying eligible patients.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Peripheral oedema is the signature toxicity of MET TKIs — anticipate it.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 32469185.
